deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a stratified space (globally, as a germ, or as a topos) with strata indexed by a poset I. For i ≤ j, the closed strata are nested, X_i ⊂ X_j. X_i^* is the open stratum and \dot X_k = X_k \ X_k^* is the boundary of a closed stratum. V̄_{X_i,X_k} is a (closed) tubular neighbourhood of X_i inside X_k. On the previous pages Grothendieck defined two kinds of 'pieces' (building blocks for a combinatorial description of the stratified space / topos):
- V_{i,k}: the neighbourhood of X_i^* in X_k, keeping the intermediate strata that contain X_i.
- V^*_{i,k}: the neighbourhood of X_i^* within the open stratum X_k^*.
He had just noted that only the 'elementary' pieces, with k a successor of i, are needed. He also noted that, under standard smoothness and normal-equisingularity hypotheses (e.g. complex algebraic Whitney-type stratifications), V^*_{ij} is a locally trivial bundle over X_i^* with fibre an open cylinder R × C_{ij}, where C_{ij} is the link.

This page. He introduces a one-parameter family of more general pieces interpolating between the two. For a chain i ≤ j ≤ k:
- (10) V^j_{i,k} := V̄_{X_i,X_k} \ (R_{j,k} ∪ S_{j,k}).
- R_{j,k} is from (3)/(3bis): the union of the closed strata X_ℓ, ℓ < k, that do not contain X_j.
- (11) S_{j,k} is the union of the X_ℓ with ℓ between j and k. The stated normalisations are S_{j,k} = ∅ if j = k and S_{j,k} = X_j if k is a successor of j. These force the range to be j ≤ ℓ < k, not 'j < ℓ ≤ k' as written.
- (12) I^{(k)} = {ℓ < k} is split into ℓ with X_ℓ ⊅ X_j (giving R_{j,k}) and ℓ with X_ℓ ⊃ X_j (giving S_{j,k}). Hence R_{j,k} ∪ S_{j,k} = \dot X_k.
- He adds the claim R_{j,k} ∩ S_{j,k} = \dot X_j (written \dot X_i).

Intended outcome (13): V^i_{i,k} = V^*_{i,k} and V^k_{i,k} = V_{i,k}, with V^i_{i,i} = X_i^*. In words, V^j_{i,k} is the neighbourhood of X_i^* in X_k from which one removes the strata lying 'below j' but keeps those between j and k. It slides from the open-stratum piece (j = i) to the closed-stratum piece (j = k).

He expects V^j_{i,k} to be, at least up to homotopy or a weakened homeomorphism notion still to be isolated, a locally trivial fibration over X_i^*. The fibres can be singular, already for V_{i,k}. The next page draws the conclusion that the general V^j_{i,k} have arbitrary singularities as fibres (take X_i a point), so they are of limited interest as 'pieces'. The programme is therefore to work with X_i^* and the elementary V_{i,j}, V^*_{i,j} (j a successor of i) first, and only later see how the V^j_{i,k} fit in.

Purpose: a combinatorial/homotopical decomposition of a stratified space (or stratified topos) into strata and normal-neighbourhood pieces with gluing data. This is a precursor of descriptions via links, holinks and exit-path data.
errors: Index range in (11) is inconsistent with the stated normalisations S_{j,k}=∅ (j=k) and S_{j,k}=X_j (k successor of j). It should read j ≤ ℓ < k, not j < ℓ ≤ k; as written S_{j,k} would contain X_k itself and V^j_{i,k} would be empty.

With the definitions as literally written, R_{j,k} ∪ S_{j,k} = \dot X_k for every j. V^j_{i,k} would then be independent of j and equal to V^*_{i,k}, contradicting V^k_{i,k} = V_{i,k} in (13). The removed set must depend on j more carefully: only strata 'below j', or relative to X_i as in (3), should be removed. Grothendieck's bookkeeping here is not yet consistent.

The claim R_{j,k} ∩ S_{j,k} = \dot X_i (presumably meant \dot X_j) is not true for general poset-stratifications. X_ℓ ∩ X_m for ℓ ≱ j ≤ m can contain strata not below j, and conversely not every stratum of \dot X_j need lie in some X_ℓ with ℓ ≱ j. At best one gets an inclusion under extra hypotheses (e.g. a frontier condition plus a lattice-like poset).
The 'homeomorphic as a locally trivial bundle over X_i^*' expectation is explicitly only heuristic; the author himself flags that a weakened notion must be found.

ideas.what: Neighbourhood pieces V_{i,k}, V^*_{i,k} of a stratum in a bigger closed or open stratum, locally trivial over X_i^* with fibre a (open) cone/cylinder on the link
ideas.modern_name: Normal slices / links in Thom–Mather stratification theory; tubular neighbourhoods with control data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970), Whitney; Goresky–MacPherson for links in stratified Morse theory
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (tame topology, 'dévissage' of stratified structures) in programmatic form

ideas.what: Interpolating family V^j_{i,k} indexed by an intermediate index j in a chain i ≤ j ≤ k: the neighbourhood of X_i^* in X_k with the strata below j removed
ideas.modern_name: Partial / relative links of a chain of strata; close to homotopy links of flags (Quinn's holinks; holinks of chains in Douteau–Waas, Haine's stratified homotopy theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (1988) homotopy links; later Miller, Woolf, Douteau, Haine, Waas for flag/chain holinks

ideas.what: Strategy: describe the stratified space using only strata and elementary pieces (j a successor of i), relegating longer chains to a second stage
ideas.modern_name: Reduction to the 'nerve' generated by covering relations of the stratification poset; local-to-global assembly of exit-path data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Exit-path category: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (Higher Algebra A.6)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes intermediate pieces V^j_{i,k} interpolating between the open-stratum link piece (j=i) and the closed-stratum piece (j=k). He also asks for a weakened notion of 'locally trivial fibration' under which they are trivial over X_i^*. This anticipates a homotopy-theoretic, stratified notion of fibration (Quinn/Hughes 'stratified approximate fibrations', holink fibrations), but the specific j-interpolation is not, to my knowledge, a standard object.
missed.quote: V^j_{i,k} a encore tendance à être homéomorphes (ou du moins, homotopes, ou homéomorphes en un sens affaibli, ou qu'il faudrait dégager...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The j-filtered family gives explicit point-set models for the mapping spaces between chain-holinks in an ∞-categorical exit-path description. It could serve as a geometric source of the face/degeneracy relations between holinks of chains of different lengths.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly bookkeeping toward a known circle of ideas (links, tubular neighbourhoods, Thom–Mather local triviality, later holinks). The interpolating V^j_{i,k} is a mildly original device, but he himself discards it on the next page, and the page contains index inconsistencies.
transcription_corrections: In (11) the subscript under the union reads 'ℓ∈I avec j<ℓ≤k' in the manuscript, but mathematically it must be j ≤ ℓ < k (consistent with the NB).
The garbled symbol before '$_{ij}$' in line 2 is likely a struck-out 'V' (or 'Z'): 'V_{ij} plus généraux que les V*_{ij}'.
'(aussi R_{j,k} ∩ S_{j,k} = \dot X_i)' — the image shows \dot X with subscript i; logically \dot X_j is intended.
The garbled symbol in the definition of I^{(k)} is a struck-out character; read I^{(k)} = {ℓ∈I | ℓ<k} (the image shows 'ℓ ≤ k' or '<k' partly overwritten).
